name: New Jersey
intro: New Jersey packs more than nine million people into suburbs, shore towns, and river cities between Philadelphia and New York, and nearly every one of its municipalities runs its own construction office. Our launch coverage starts with the eight big commuter counties of North and Central Jersey — Bergen, Essex, Middlesex, Hudson, Monmouth, Ocean, Union, and Morris.
licensingNotes: Home-improvement contractors must register with the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs (HIC registration), and licensed trades — electricians, plumbers, HVACR — carry state license numbers you can look up in the DCA's MyLicense system. Building permits are issued by each municipality's construction office under the statewide Uniform Construction Code.

name: New York
intro: Our New York coverage starts downstate: the five boroughs plus Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester, and Rockland — the territory where most tri-state hiring decisions happen. Licensing here is famously fragmented, which is exactly why we verify it.
licensingNotes: In the five boroughs, home-improvement contractors are licensed by the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, and building work runs through the NYC Department of Buildings. Nassau, Suffolk, Westchester, and Rockland each license contractors through county consumer-affairs offices, and many trades are licensed town by town. State-licensed professions are verifiable through the NYS Office of the Professions.

name: Pennsylvania
intro: Our Pennsylvania coverage starts in the southeast: Philadelphia and its four collar counties — Montgomery, Bucks, Delaware, and Chester. Housing here runs from Philadelphia rowhomes to Main Line estates to postwar suburbs, and contractor rules change at the county line.
licensingNotes: Home-improvement contractors must register with the Pennsylvania Attorney General under HICPA — note the AG's own caveat that registration is not an endorsement of competency. Licensed professions are verifiable in the state PALS system, and Philadelphia runs its own trade licensing through the Department of Licenses and Inspections.
